Conversely, outcomes could surge above the upper bounds if there are unexpectedly strong positive developments, such as a breakthrough innovation, a highly positive earnings surprise that significantly alters future expectations, an unanticipated economic boom, or a sudden, widespread surge in investor confidence. These types of "black swan" or major catalytic events are inherently difficult to predict and thus lie outside the scope of typical probabilistic modeling.
